question: An email to all staff, in the style layoff notices are often written. What is it telling them?
answer: That some of them are being sacked. In 1946 George Orwell noted that political language names things without calling up pictures of them, because the plain description would be too ugly to say. Here roles are impacted, so no person is fired and nobody does the firing. A camera would show a desk being cleared.
move: When a word hides a picture, describe what a camera would show.
ask: Which soft word do I use to avoid picturing what I am really doing?

scene.head: Message to all staff
scene.title: Positioning us for growth
scene.body: As part of our strategic realignment, we are rightsizing the organisation. Some roles will be impacted, and affected colleagues will be supported through this transition.

phrases.why: Strategy words put a plan where a decision was. Nobody has to picture anything.
Right implies the old size was a mistake. Nobody chose the word by accident.

phrases.plain: Some of you will lose your jobs
phrases.why: Roles, not people; impacted, not fired. The grammar hides who acts and who suffers.
Transition sounds like a journey. Here the journey is out of the door.

scene.ask: One phrase is about the reader's own job. Which?
scene.watch: When a sentence has nobody doing anything, ask who does what to whom.

source: Orwell, Politics and the English Language, 1946
reference: Orwell, Politics and the English Language, Horizon 13(76), 1946
